chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who is making up the month of Ramadan, and her husband forces her to break the fast. He said: 'It is not appropriate for him to force her after midday (Zawal).'

key_terms.بَعْدَ الزَّوَالِ: After midday (when the sun passes its zenith)
key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up the missed fasts of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Can a husband force his wife to break her Ramadan make-up fast?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the juristic debate on whether a husband’s right to conjugal intimacy overrides a wife’s obligatory make-up fasts. The narration specifies that after midday (Zawal), when the fast is already established, the husband cannot compel her to break it, thereby prioritizing the completion of her religious duty over his claim during the latter part of the day.
